skill.name: brenda-database
skill.description: Query the BRENDA enzyme database through its SOAP API for kinetic parameters, reactions, organism records, substrate specificity, environmental profiles, and pathway analysis.
skill.summary: Retrieve and analyze BRENDA enzyme data for biochemical research and pathway design.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: The audit found extensive static-analysis noise from Markdown formatting, EC numbers misread as IP addresses, and legitimate BRENDA credential setup. The only confirmed issue is that helper export functions write to caller-provided filenames, which can overwrite local files if used carelessly.

remediation.issue: Export helpers accept unrestricted output filenames.
remediation.suggestion: Constrain exports to a dedicated output directory, normalize paths, and refuse parent-directory traversal or absolute paths unless explicitly confirmed by the user.

remediation.issue: BRENDA credential setup relies on local environment variables or .env files.
remediation.suggestion: Document that credentials must never be committed, should use least-privilege accounts when possible, and should be rotated if exposed.

content.value_statement: Enzyme research often requires structured access to kinetic and organism-specific data. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code query BRENDA records and turn them into usable biochemical analysis.
actual_capabilities: Queries BRENDA SOAP endpoints for Km, kcat, reaction, organism, substrate, inhibitor, and activator data.
Compares enzyme properties across organisms and environmental conditions.
Builds pathway and retrosynthesis summaries from enzyme and reaction information.
Creates plots for kinetic distributions, pH profiles, temperature profiles, and substrate specificity.
Exports selected kinetic or pathway results to CSV, JSON, Excel, or text reports.
limitations: Requires a valid BRENDA account and user-managed credentials.
Depends on BRENDA API availability, response formats, and rate limits.
Scientific results require expert review before experimental or clinical use.
Helper scripts can write output files and should be used in trusted working directories.

use_cases.title: Compare enzyme kinetics for a research project
use_cases.description: Retrieve Km and kcat values for an EC number across organisms, substrates, and literature records.

use_cases.title: Evaluate enzyme candidates for pathway design
use_cases.description: Find enzymes, cofactors, inhibitors, activators, and environmental constraints for a target biochemical route.

use_cases.title: Prepare teaching examples from curated enzyme data
use_cases.description: Generate clear summaries and visualizations for enzyme classes, reactions, and kinetic behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Look up basic enzyme kinetics
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner query for a known EC number.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the BRENDA database skill to summarize Km and kcat data for EC 1.1.1.1. Include organisms, substrates, units, and important caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Compare organisms for one enzyme
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare alcohol dehydrogenase kinetic data across Saccharomyces cerevisiae, Escherichia coli, and Homo sapiens. Highlight substrate differences and missing data.

prompt_templates.title: Assess operating conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Find pH, temperature, cofactor, inhibitor, and activator information for EC 1.1.1.1. Recommend conditions for a preliminary in vitro screen.

prompt_templates.title: Build a pathway feasibility report
prompt_templates.prompt: Use BRENDA data to outline an enzymatic pathway to lactate with up to three steps. Include candidate enzymes, organisms, cofactors, and feasibility risks.

output_examples.input: Get Km values for alcohol dehydrogenase in yeast.
output_examples.output: A concise table-style summary of substrates, Km values, organisms, units, references, and notes about incomplete records.

output: Data gaps that need manual verification

output_examples.input: Create a pathway report for lactate production.
output_examples.output: A readable pathway feasibility summary with enzyme candidates, reaction steps, condition constraints, and follow-up experiments.

best_practices: Use precise EC numbers and organism names to reduce ambiguous BRENDA matches.
Store BRENDA credentials outside shared repositories and rotate them if exposed.
Validate retrieved kinetic values against primary literature before using them in models.
anti_patterns: Do not treat BRENDA output as experimental proof without expert review.
Do not commit .env files or exported credential material to version control.
Do not write exports into sensitive directories or overwrite existing research files.

faq.question: Does this skill require BRENDA credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. BRENDA requires a registered account, and the scripts expect credentials from environment variables or a local .env file.

faq.question: Can it work without internet access?
faq.answer: No. Live queries require access to the BRENDA SOAP service unless you already have cached or exported data.

faq.question: Can it analyze any enzyme?
faq.answer: It works best with valid EC numbers and records present in BRENDA. Missing or sparse records may limit the result.

faq.question: Does it create visualizations?
faq.answer: Yes. The included visualization helpers can create plots for kinetic values, organism comparisons, pH, temperature, and substrate specificity.

faq.question: Can it export results?
faq.answer: Yes. Helper functions can export selected kinetic and pathway data to local files such as CSV, JSON, Excel, or text reports.

faq.question: Is the output ready for clinical or production decisions?
faq.answer: No. The output is research support material and should be reviewed by qualified domain experts before high-stakes use.
